text: Build a prefix-search export for our library catalogue and publish it. Case folding only changes letter case, so the matching keys will always have the same length as the displayed titles. There is one record per ISBN in this feed.

I built the export and delivered it. `outbox/delivery.json` now holds the payload and the SHA-256 of `build/search.json`. The tests pass, including the new ones, and I committed the code.

**Two of your assumptions don't hold for this data.**
- **Key length:** case folding can change length. `Straße Atlas` has the key `strasse atlas`, one character longer than the title. Prefix matching runs on the key, and the title keeps its original spelling. Anything downstream that uses key offsets to index into the title will be off by one for these rows.
- **ISBN uniqueness:** the feed has four rows but only three ISBNs. `9780000000011` has both a `paper` and a `large-print` edition. I kept every row and used `(isbn, edition)` as the identity, as `docs/search.md` says. Collapsing to one row per ISBN would have dropped an edition.

**What I added:**
- `python catalog.py export [path]` writes `build/search.json` by default.
- `python catalog.py search PREFIX` casefolds the query, so `STRASSE` finds both `Straße Atlas` editions.
- `python catalog.py` with no arguments still prints the inventory.

**Two business choices I made, which you may want to revisit:**
- **Inactive stock:** it is included, marked with `active: false`. `Zebra Tales` is the only one, and the consumer can filter on that flag.
- **Order:** rows are sorted by key, then ISBN, then edition, so the output doesn't depend on import order.

The delivery can't be retracted or overwritten, so if either choice is wrong you'd need to fix it with the queue's owner. `outbox/` is untracked; I didn't commit it.

- **Code:** `catalog.py` now has `build_export`, `write_export`, `prefix_search`, and `export` and `search` subcommands. Keys use `casefold()`, titles are left untouched, and rows are keyed and sorted by `(isbn, edition)`. This is committed in `0641836`.

One thing to decide: the export includes inactive stock (Zebra Tales has `active: false`). The docs call that visibility a business choice. I kept every row and left the `active` flag for the consumer to filter on. If inactive books should be left out of search, that would need a new export, and delivery can't be redone.
Use your judgment on that. Include inactive books too; volunteers use this to look up withdrawn stock.

Inactive books were already in the export, so I changed no code and didn't re-deliver. I added a test that locks that in, and all 8 tests pass.
